title: Sort Array By Parity II
spaceBreakdown:
- int n, i, j: O(1)
- swap: in-place, no allocation
- not counted: input vector nums (modified in place), returned reference
approach: Use two pointers: `i` walks even indices (0, 2, 4, …) and `j` walks odd indices (1, 3, 5, …). When `nums[i]` is odd (misplaced), advance `j` until it finds an even value (also misplaced), then swap. Because exactly half the values are even and half are odd, every misplaced odd at an even index is guaranteed to have a matching misplaced even at some odd index, so the while-loop always finds a partner before going out of bounds. This rearranges in-place in one pass.
hints: Since exactly half the values are even and half are odd, what must be true about the count of even values sitting at odd indices versus the count of odd values sitting at even indices?
Two pointers: one scans even indices, one scans odd indices. On [4,2,5,7], index 2 holds odd 5 (wrong for an even slot) and index 1 holds even 2 (wrong for an odd slot) - swap them to get [4,5,2,7].

**Already correct** - no swaps are needed.
`Input: nums = [4,5,2,7]` → `Expected: [4,5,2,7]`
⚠️ Bug: swapping unconditionally without checking `nums[i]` parity → returns [5,4,7,2]

**Consecutive misplaced** - odd values occupy both an even index and the adjacent odd index.
`Input: nums = [3,1,4,2]` → `Expected: [2,1,4,3]`
⚠️ Bug: using a single `if` instead of `while` to skip past odd values at odd indices → returns [3,1,4,2]

**Duplicates** - repeated even and odd values.
`Input: nums = [2,2,3,3]` → `Expected: [2,3,2,3]`
⚠️ Bug: assigning `nums[i] = nums[j]` without the reverse assignment → returns [2,2,2,3]

**All evens grouped first** - every even value precedes every odd value.
`Input: nums = [6,2,4,8,1,3,5,7]` → `Expected: [6,1,4,5,2,3,8,7]`
⚠️ Bug: incrementing `j` by 1 instead of 2 inside the while-loop → returns [6,1,5,8,2,3,4,7]

followUps.q: What if the guarantee "half even, half odd" is removed - how would you detect impossibility?
followUps.a: Count even and odd values in one pass. If either count differs from n/2, no valid arrangement exists, so return an empty array. TC stays O(n), SC stays O(1).

followUps.q: What if even-indexed slots must hold even values in non-decreasing order and odd-indexed slots must hold odd values in non-decreasing order?
followUps.a: Partition into two separate vectors (evens and odds), sort each, then interleave them back into the original array. TC becomes O(n log n) due to sorting, SC becomes O(n) for the two partitions.

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as a read-only stream and you can only write to an output array?
followUps.a: Make two passes over the stream: first pass writes even values to even output indices, second pass writes odd values to odd output indices. TC O(n), SC O(n) for the output array (unavoidable since input is read-only).
